statement_record.book: Prop 8.17: for any small category C, the presheaf category Sets^(C^op) is a topos. evidence.intree_statement: Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.  (* forward = char, backward = pullback of `truth` along h; both round trips proved, Defined so it computes *)

Definition relations_iso {C : Category} {H : ElementaryTopos C} (a b : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj (a × b) |} {| carrier := a ~> Pow b |} := iso_compose exp_iso (classifier_classifies (a × b)).  (* Pow b := Ω ^ b, so this is the power-object reading Sub(a × b) ≅ (a ~> Ω^b) *)

char_pullback {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one;  (* field of Class SubobjectClassifier; its UMP is exactly the membership criterion — any z ~> x with char m ∘ z ≈ truth ∘ one factors uniquely through m *)

statement_record.book: Remark 8.18: since subobjects U >-> E correspond to arrows u : E → Omega, Omega is an object of truth values with t = 'true', u is a propositional function and U its extension; the classifying pullback yields the membership criterion U = {x ∈ E : u x = true} for generalized elements x : X → E; topoi further model first-order quantifiers as adjoints to pullback, and cartesian closure plus the classifier interprets higher-order logic, with Omega^E the power object P(E).
statement_record.intree: The subobject/characteristic-map correspondence is a theorem (classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) in Sets), Ω and truth are the class data, the power object is Pow a := Ω ^ a with relations_iso : SubObj (a × b) ≅ (a ~> Pow b), and the membership criterion is available as the universal property of the classifying pullback square char_pullback (not as a named lemma about generalized elements).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the logical half: the two set-theoretic clauses (subobject ⟺ characteristic map; Ω^E as the object of subobjects of E) are present at full strength — indeed classifier_classifies is an isomorphism of setoids, stronger than the book's bijection of classes, and it is proved for an arbitrary category with terminal + pullbacks. The membership criterion is only implicit in char_pullback's UMP rather than stated in Awodey's generalized-element form. The quantifier and higher-order-logic clauses have no in-tree counterpart at all.

statement_record.book: Exercise 5: use the Yoneda Lemma to show that for any set A the functor A × − : Sets → Sets preserves ALL colimits, i.e. A × colim_i B_i ≅ colim_i (A × B_i) for any diagram i : I → Sets.
statement_record.intree: Only the finite-coproduct instances of the conclusion, and stated as distributivity rather than as colimit preservation: prod_coprod_r : x × (y + z) ≅ x × y + x × z and prod_zero_r : x × 0 ≅ 0, both derived from Cartesian + Cocartesian + Closed and hence available at Sets. The file header of Structure/BiCCC.v gives exactly the book's reason ('because the category is closed, each functor _ × x has a right adjoint _ ^ x, hence preserves all colimits'), but that general statement is not proved.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the shapes `two-object discrete` and `empty` are covered, not arbitrary diagrams; and even those are phrased as isomorphisms of objects, not as a `PreservesColimit` witness. In-tree the result is more general in the ambient category (any bicartesian closed C, not just Sets).
